items.title: Psilocybin's effect on human brain synaptic plasticity.
items.summary_en: Single-dose psilocybin study (0.3 mg/kg, n=15) measured synaptic density changes via PET imaging in frontal cortex and hippocampus. No significant overall increase in synaptic markers was found. However, participants in therapeutic-like settings reported stronger mystical experiences and greater synaptic density increases than those in MRI scanners, suggesting environmental context modulates psilocybin's neuroplastic effects.

items.title: From Schedule I to the Clinic-Insights Into Psychedelic Drug Development From GHB.
items.summary_en: This viewpoint examines sodium oxybate (GHB) as a case study for how Schedule I substances, including psychedelics, can navigate regulatory pathways toward clinical approval. The analysis illustrates regulatory mechanisms that may apply to psychedelic drug development.

items.title: Micro-phenomenology of immersion and perceived presences under DMT.
items.summary_en: Study of 23 participants receiving 20 mg intravenous DMT with concurrent fMRI-EEG monitoring characterized immersion as a structured continuum using micro-phenomenological analysis. Detailed interviews identified 125 phenomenological categories across sensory, spatial, and social dimensions. Results show immersion develops hierarchically: bodily effects precede visual and auditory experiences, with perceived presences emerging only after multisensory integration and 3D spatial development.
items.notable_reason: First-in-human application of micro-phenomenology to DMT with simultaneous neuroimaging acquisition and detailed temporal analysis of immersive experience structure.

items.title: Ionic Homeostasis Failure in Major Depressive Disorder: Ion Channel Mechanisms, Excitation-Inhibition Imbalance, and Precision Therapeutics.
items.summary_en: A new framework proposes that major depressive disorder involves widespread failure of ionic homeostasis in neurons and glial cells. Genetic factors, chronic stress, and neuroinflammation disrupt calcium, potassium, and chloride balance, leading to excitation-inhibition imbalance and network instability. The review identifies key ion channels (CACNA1C, TREK-1, KCNQ, others) as therapeutic targets and discusses how ketamine, chloride-restoring drugs, and AI-guided approaches may enable precision treatments.

items.title: Backed by $11M NIDA Grant, Harvard Moves Forward on Ibogaine for Opioid Use Disorder Research
items.summary_en: Harvard receives an $11 million NIDA grant to advance multi-phase research on ibogaine for opioid use disorder treatment. The funding supports clinical development of this psychedelic compound as a potential therapeutic intervention, with additional support opportunities announced by ARPA-H.
items.notable_reason: Significant federal funding ($11M NIDA grant) for ibogaine clinical research at major institution, representing major policy/funding development in psychedelic medicine.

items.title: Acute Hallucinogen Intoxication Following Ingestion of a Commercially Available Mushroom Extract Product: A Case Report.
items.summary_en: Case report of an 18-year-old female presenting to emergency care with acute hallucinogenic intoxication after consuming a commercially available mushroom extract product. Clinical presentation included severe anxiety, agitation, visual and auditory hallucinations, paranoid ideation, and autonomic symptoms. Examination revealed tachycardia, tachypnea, dilated pupils, and psychomotor agitation. Diagnostic workup excluded co-ingestion and end-organ damage. The case highlights regulatory gaps in mushroom product labeling and potential psilocybin contamination in retail supplements.

items.title: Psychedelic therapy at the end of life: unexplored alternative to assisted suicide in the UK.
items.summary_en: Editorial examining psychedelic therapy as a potential alternative to assisted suicide in end-of-life care. Evidence suggests psychedelics reduce existential distress and suicidality in terminal patients. Author argues for rescheduling these substances to enable research on their role in palliative care before implementing assisted suicide policy in the UK.

items.title: Longitudinal dream-content shift and void-like dissociative phenomenology around outpatient ketamine infusions in chronic low back pain: a case report.
items.summary_en: Case report documenting dream content changes in a 48-year-old man with chronic low back pain over 16 years, including five low-dose ketamine infusions (15 mg) in 2014. Analysis of 50 masked dream narratives using a pre-specified coding scheme showed decreased obstruction motifs and increased social-interaction themes post-ketamine. Findings suggest possible links between ketamine's dissociative phenomenology and longer-term imaginal processes, without efficacy claims.

items.title: Combined DMT-harmine formulation reduces negative self-referential emotions during social self-evaluation: a randomized placebo-controlled trial in healthy volunteers.
items.summary_en: Randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial (N=28) examining combined DMT-harmine on self-referential emotions. Participants rated embarrassment and shame while listening to recordings of their own singing versus control vocals using visual analogue scales and the Experiential Shame Scale. HAR/DMT significantly reduced embarrassment compared to placebo in self-listening condition (p=.001), with no effect in control conditions. Harmine alone showed no significant effects.

items.title: Acceptability and safety of two sequential doses of psilocybin in bipolar II depression: protocol for an open-label single-arm feasibility study.
items.summary_en: Open-label feasibility study examining acceptability and safety of two sequential 25 mg psilocybin doses in 10 patients with bipolar II depression and suicidal ideation. Doses given 4 weeks apart with structured psychotherapy based on mindfulness cognitive-behavioural therapy. Addresses treatment gap in bipolar II, where standard pharmacotherapy often proves inadequate.

items.title: Enhancing plasticity to treat depression and other central nervous system diseases using event-driven pharmacology.
items.summary_en: Event-driven pharmacology proposes that plastogens—substances including ketamine and classical psychedelics—produce sustained neuroplastic effects from brief drug exposure, contrasting traditional occupancy-driven models. These compounds activate synaptic machinery and metaplasticity, potentially offering rapid-acting antidepressant benefits with fewer side effects than drugs requiring prolonged receptor occupancy.

items.title: Keeping Up with the Feds: From FDA to HRSA, Washington Backs Psychedelics
items.summary_en: US federal agencies including the FDA and HRSA are increasing support for psychedelic research and therapeutic development. This institutional backing signals growing recognition of hallucinogens' potential in clinical settings, reflecting a shift in regulatory approach toward these compounds.

items.title: FDA Issues Final Psychedelics Guidance, Schedules September Hearing on the Future of Psychedelic Therapies
items.summary_en: The FDA has issued final guidance on clinical investigations of psychedelics, building on a June 2023 draft document. The 11-page guidance covers nonclinical research, chemistry and manufacturing, clinical studies, and abuse potential assessments. After three years of stakeholder feedback, the FDA has scheduled a September hearing to discuss the future direction of psychedelic therapies.
items.notable_reason: FDA issues first formal guidance document on psychedelic clinical investigations, a national-level regulatory milestone affecting the entire field.

items.title: Changes in trauma symptoms of discrimination after MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder.
items.summary_en: A preliminary study (n=5) examined MDMA-assisted therapy for trauma symptoms related to discrimination using the Trauma Symptoms of Discrimination Scale. Paired t-test showed a 38% reduction in scores (p=.046, Cohen's d=1.28). All participants reported marked improvements across diverse racial/ethnic backgrounds and discrimination histories. Results suggest MDMA-assisted therapy may reduce discrimination-related trauma in marginalized populations, though larger studies are needed.

items.title: Brain-targeted epigenetic effects of two emerging psychoplastogens: ketamine & MDMA.
items.summary_en: Brain-targeted epigenetic study examined DNA methylation changes in 20 ketamine and 16 MDMA clinical trial participants. Both psychoplastogens altered 300+ genes each, with convergent effects on neuroplasticity and neuroimmune pathways. Blood and saliva samples analyzed pre/post-treatment using linear mixed-effects models reveal peripheral epigenetic mechanisms underlying therapeutic effects for mood and trauma disorders.

items.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy in treatment-resistant depression: rapid remission, uncertain durability, and the next phase of clinical evidence.
items.summary_en: Psilocybin-assisted therapy shows rapid symptom reduction in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), but long-term durability remains unclear. Early randomized trials demonstrate promising short-term remission rates, yet evidence is limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and inadequate comparison with established TRD treatments like esketamine and electroconvulsive therapy. Key questions about sustained benefit and effects of repeated dosing remain unanswered.

items.title: Epigenetic landscapes of classical psychedelics and ketamine: molecular mechanisms of long-lasting neuromodulation.
items.summary_en: Review examining how classical psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, mescaline) and ketamine produce lasting neuroplastic changes through epigenetic mechanisms. Evidence suggests therapeutic effects in neuropsychiatric conditions involve DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin restructuring, and non-coding RNA dynamics. Psychedelics modulate metabolic pathways affecting epigenetic cofactors, potentially driving persistent transcriptional changes and enhanced synaptic connectivity, though direct causal evidence remains limited.

items.title: Psychedelics and the thalamocortical system: A scoping review.
items.summary_en: A scoping review examined how psychedelics affect the thalamocortical system, synthesizing preclinical and clinical evidence using PRISMA methodology. The review focused on NMDA antagonists, serotonin 2A agonists, and iboga alkaloids. Psychedelics show therapeutic promise for depression, trauma, OCD, and substance use disorder. Since several psychiatric conditions—depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, autism—involve thalamocortical alterations, understanding thalamic function could advance psychedelic research and biological psychiatry.

items.title: Personality changes following first-time psychedelic use in college students in Germany.
items.summary_en: A one-year longitudinal study of 102 first-time psychedelic users and 1,066 controls among Berlin university students found small increases in Openness and decreases in Conscientiousness (Big Five Inventory), though effects were modest and attenuated after adjusting for confounders. Changes were not clearly distinct from other first-time illicit substance users. Participants with psychiatric diagnoses showed larger Neuroticism reductions. Causal interpretability remains limited.

items.title: Navigating 'k-land': a qualitative exploration of participants' experiences of ketamine-assisted psychotherapy for methamphetamine use disorder.
items.summary_en: Qualitative study of 14 participants in an open-label pilot trial examining experiences of ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP) for methamphetamine use disorder. Semi-structured interviews identified four themes: prior limited treatment success prompting openness to novel approaches; importance of relational safety and clinical containment; reduced emotional reactivity following ketamine sessions; and translation of psychological shifts into behavioral change. Findings suggest KAP acceptability and potential mechanisms in this population.

items.title: Psychedelics in Mental Health: Opportunities and Challenges.
items.summary_en: A special issue examines psychedelics' potential in treating depression, PTSD, and substance disorders. While early trials show promise, key questions remain about mechanisms, safety, and ethics. Research emphasizes that psychedelic therapy involves more than pharmacology: therapeutic relationships, preparation, integration, and cultural context significantly influence outcomes. Subjective experience and meaning-making appear central to therapeutic change.

items.title: Convergent increases in serotonin 1B receptor binding following ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy: a multi-centre bayesian re-analysis of PET data.
items.summary_en: A multi-centre Bayesian re-analysis of PET imaging data found convergent increases in serotonin 1B receptor binding following both ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). The study used PET neuroimaging to measure in vivo serotonin 1B receptor availability, suggesting these two distinct antidepressant treatments may share a common neurobiological mechanism.

items.title: Pα+ Psychedelic Bulletin #227: A Closer Look at Compass’ 6-Month Data; AtaiBeckley Deal Update; ‘Rysanso’ Brand MDMA?
items.summary_en: Pα+ Psychedelic Bulletin #227: A Closer Look at Compass’ 6-Month Data; AtaiBeckley Deal Update; ‘Rysanso’ Brand MDMA?
items.notable_reason: Phase 3 pivotal trial (COMP360/COMP006) 6-month data readout with regulatory pathway implications for potential FDA approval.

items.title: Blinding integrity in psychedelic research: Evidence from a comparative randomized controlled trial of psilocybin, MDMA, and methylphenidate in healthy volunteers
items.summary_en: Blinding integrity in psychedelic research: Evidence from a comparative randomized controlled trial of psilocybin, MDMA, and methylphenidate in healthy volunteers

items.title: Intensity and Visual Content Dissociate in DMT: Dynamic Integration-Complexity Predicts One, Spatial Configuration the Other
items.summary_en: EEG study (N=35) in inhaled DMT identifies a novel measure (mac_I) tracking dynamic integration-complexity changes that predicts subjective experience intensity (ρ=0.41, p=0.016), distinct from content. Microstate spatial configuration predicts visual imagery type (ρ=0.56, p<0.001) independently of intensity, forming a pre-specified double dissociation (p=0.007). Results were DMT-specific and did not generalize to psilocybin (N=57).

items.title: Lifetime psychedelic use and opioid use disorder severity in a National Survey: the roles of psychedelic type and mental health
items.summary_en: Cross-sectional analysis of 45,133 U.S. adults using structural equation modeling found divergent associations between psychedelic use and opioid use disorder (OUD) severity. Mescaline/peyote use correlated with lower OUD severity (β=-0.34), while LSD/psilocybin/MDMA/DMT use correlated with higher severity (β=0.60). Mental health impairment moderated these relationships: mescaline/peyote's protective association emerged only in those with high mental health impairment, whereas the adverse association for other psychedelics was attenuated in this group.

items.title: Psychedelics for treatment of negative symptoms and depressive symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorder: A narrative review
items.summary_en: Narrative review examining whether serotonergic psychedelics could treat depressive and negative symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. Both conditions involve dopamine, glutamate, and neuroplasticity disturbances. Preclinical evidence shows psychedelics increase dendritic spine density, enhance BDNF, and modulate network connectivity, suggesting potential therapeutic relevance for addressing maladaptive brain networks in schizophrenia.

items.title: Classic psychedelics and personality: An updated systematic review
items.summary_en: Updated systematic review (2016–2024) examining how classic psychedelics (5-HT2A agonists) affect personality traits. Analysis of randomized controlled trials, open-label, and observational studies across four databases, using validated personality assessment instruments. Contradictory prior findings suggest need for systematic evaluation of mechanisms underlying personality changes linked to serotonergic receptor agonism.
items.notable_reason: Updated systematic review (2016–2024) on classic psychedelics and personality traits, synthesizing evidence across multiple compounds and study designs.

items.title: A systematic review of the pharmacokinetics of classical serotonergic psychedelic compounds in healthy adult subjects
items.summary_en: Systematic review of 32 trials examining pharmacokinetics of classical serotonergic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, mescaline, 5-MeO-DMT) in healthy adults. LSD most studied, followed by DMT across intravenous and oral routes. Key findings: dose-proportional peak concentrations for LSD and psilocybin; notable differences between administration routes.
items.notable_reason: Systematic review synthesizing pharmacokinetic data across 32 trials of multiple classical psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, mescaline, 5-MEO-DMT), providing foundational neuroscience understanding for clinical development.

items.title: Association between Intravenous Ketamine Treatment and Cognitive Function in Patients with Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
items.summary_en: Double-blind RCT (N=34) examining ketamine's effects on cognitive function in treatment-resistant depression. Intravenous ketamine (0.5 mg/kg, 4 doses) produced no significant differences versus placebo on objective or subjective cognitive measures. Ketamine responders showed improved subjective cognition versus non-responders. Baseline inhibitory control deficits predicted greater antidepressant response.

items.title: CSF galanin and noradrenaline downregulation by psilocybin therapy in major depressive disorder.
items.summary_en: Secondary analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled trial examined cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers following psilocybin therapy in major depressive disorder. Psilocybin selectively reduced CSF galanin and noradrenaline levels, suggesting that normalization of these co-transmitters may represent a key mechanism underlying its rapid antidepressant effects.

items.title: Psilocybin therapy for adult females with anorexia nervosa: pilot study.
items.summary_en: Pilot study of psilocybin therapy in 21 adult females with anorexia nervosa. Single-blind design with three oral psilocybin sessions (1 mg, 25 mg, 25 mg) over 6 weeks plus talk therapy. Primary outcomes: Eating Disorder Examination and motivation scores at 6 weeks, 3 and 6 months. Psilocybin was well tolerated; common adverse events were headache, nausea, dizziness. One participant reported two suicide attempts. Results suggest potential feasibility and safety for further investigation.

items.title: Compass Closes Out Phase 3 With 6-Month COMP006 Data, Eyes H1’27 Launch
items.summary_en: Compass Pathways released 26-week data from COMP006, a Phase 3 trial (n=581) evaluating COMP360 psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression. Participants received two doses of 1 mg, 10 mg, or 25 mg psilocybin three weeks apart. The company targets H1 2027 for a potential market launch.
items.notable_reason: Phase 3 pivotal trial (n=581) with 6-month follow-up data and H1'27 launch timeline suggests imminent regulatory decision/approval pathway.

items.title: MDMA-assisted PTSD and Alcohol Therapy Trial (MPATHY): study protocol for a double-blind, randomised, controlled outpatient trial of MDMA-assisted integrated exposure-based therapy for comorbid post-traumatic stress disorder and alcohol use disorder.
items.summary_en: MDMA-assisted PTSD and Alcohol Therapy Trial (MPATHY): study protocol for a double-blind, randomised, controlled outpatient trial of MDMA-assisted integrated exposure-based therapy for comorbid post-traumatic stress disorder and alcohol use disorder.
items.notable_reason: World-first double-blind RCT examining MDMA-assisted integrated exposure therapy for comorbid PTSD+AUD, n=100, with cost-effectiveness analysis and rigorous biomarker validation (phosphatidylethanol).

items.title: Policy pathways and historical insights: Canada's evolving approach to psychedelic access for end-of-life distress.
items.summary_en: Canada is shifting from prohibitionist drug policies toward recognizing psychedelics' therapeutic potential for end-of-life distress in palliative care. This policy evolution mirrors international trends in the US, Australia, and Europe. Canada's existing frameworks for holistic end-of-life care, medical assistance in dying, compassionate access mechanisms, and patient advocacy positions it uniquely for clinical integration of psychedelics in palliative settings, though heterogeneous provincial regulations remain.

items.title: Ketamine alters the aperiodic EEG exponent in major depression: implications for cortical E/I balance and treatment prediction.
items.summary_en: Placebo-controlled study (n=24) examined ketamine's effects on EEG aperiodic exponent in major depression. Subanesthetic ketamine (0.54 mg/kg IV) significantly reduced the aperiodic exponent, a marker of cortical excitation-inhibition balance. Higher pretreatment occipital aperiodic exponent predicted antidepressant response at 24 hours. Findings suggest EEG aperiodic exponent as a potential biomarker for ketamine treatment outcomes in treatment-resistant depression.

items.title: Effectiveness and safety of repeat dose subcutaneous ketamine for treatment-resistant depression, and the impact of prior ketamine treatment: open label extension of the KADS study.
items.summary_en: Open-label extension of the KADS trial examined repeated subcutaneous ketamine for treatment-resistant depression. 130 participants received twice-weekly injections (0.5-0.9 mg/kg) for 4 weeks across seven Australasian centres. At treatment end, 30% showed ≥50% symptom reduction; only 17% maintained response at 4-week follow-up. Over 50% showed minimal improvement. Prior ketamine exposure produced transiently reduced initial response but outcomes converged. Safety and longer-term efficacy data remain limited.

items.title: Kynurenine pathway profiles as markers of ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression.
items.summary_en: Study of 30 treatment-resistant depression patients receiving six intravenous ketamine infusions over three weeks. Researchers measured kynurenine pathway metabolites (tryptophan, kynurenine, kynurenic acid, 3-hydroxykynurenine, quinolinic acid) at baseline, day 3, and day 18, correlating levels with depression severity via MADRS scale. Higher baseline kynurenic acid associated with greater symptom improvement by day 18, suggesting kynurenine pathway profiles may serve as biomarkers for predicting ketamine response.

items.title: High-order brain interactions during ketamine-induced state changes: A functional marker of response in late-life treatment-resistant depression?
items.summary_en: This secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blind trial examined brain activity patterns in 30 late-life veterans with treatment-resistant depression following ketamine or midazolam infusion. Using EEG-derived high-order interactions, researchers found ketamine induced dynamic changes in brain redundancy, with peak effects in the alpha band at 1 hour. Greater increases in alpha-band redundancy at 24 hours correlated with improved depressive symptoms at day 7, suggesting these neural markers may help identify ketamine responders.

items.title: Single Ayahuasca administration attenuates alcohol relapse and associated behavioral, neurochemical, and oxidative alterations in rats.
items.summary_en: Rat study demonstrates single ayahuasca dose reduces alcohol relapse and anxiety-like behavior following 35-day ethanol exposure. Treatment (2.72 mg/kg DMT + β-carbolines) decreased relapse drinking, normalized dopamine/serotonin levels, elevated BDNF, and restored antioxidant enzyme activity in frontal cortex, hippocampus, and striatum versus controls.

items.title: Toward a nuanced framework for the Medical development of ibogaine and its analogues and derivatives: implications for psychopharmacology.
items.summary_en: This review proposes a framework for developing ibogaine analogs and derivatives as therapeutics for substance use disorders, trauma, mood disorders, and suicidality. Two strategies are distinguished: preserving ibogaine's broad polypharmacological effects while reducing safety risks, or creating selective analogs targeting specific conditions (OUD, TBI, PTSD). The authors evaluate evidence for each approach and discuss trade-offs in safety, efficacy, and scalability, emphasizing the need to account for individual pharmacogenetic variability.

items.title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of pharmacological interventions for postpartum depression: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
items.summary_en: Network meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (N=1722) comparing pharmacological treatments for postpartum depression. Saffron, fluoxetine, esketamine, brexanolone, and zuranolone showed symptom improvement versus placebo. Fluoxetine, saffron, and zuranolone had higher response rates; brexanolone alone demonstrated significant remission improvement. Brexanolone showed poor acceptability; zuranolone increased adverse events. Evidence quality mostly low-to-moderate.

items.title: Mitochondrial-inflammation crosstalk in major depressive disorder: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
items.summary_en: Recent research identifies mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation as central to major depressive disorder. Mitochondrial defects impair energy production and trigger inflammatory responses, creating a self-reinforcing cycle. Studies show conventional antidepressants gradually restore mitochondrial function, while ketamine induces rapid metabolic changes. Psychedelics and mitochondria-targeted compounds show additional therapeutic promise through this mechanistic pathway.

items.title: Effects of sub-anesthetic doses of esketamine on immune function and postoperative negative emotions in acoustic neuroma patients: a randomized clinical trial.
items.summary_en: Effects of sub-anesthetic doses of esketamine on immune function and postoperative negative emotions in acoustic neuroma patients: a randomized clinical trial.

items.title: Insights into psilocybin use among people with bipolar disorder: A thematic analysis of Reddit posts
items.summary_en: Thematic analysis of 354 Reddit posts examining psilocybin use among people with bipolar disorder. Study identified four themes: mania, depression, mixed experiences, and broader perspectives. While some reported reduced depression and cognitive shifts, others experienced increased or new mania, psychosis, and worsening depression. Findings suggest psilocybin may benefit some individuals but carries risks requiring careful consideration.

items.summary_en: Psilocin mediates long-term synaptic depression in the prelimbic cortex through 5-HT2A receptor-independent mechanisms

items.title: Insights from the psychedelic experience integration session: Verbatims differentiate 3-month abstinence in alcohol use disorder with depressive symptoms
items.summary_en: Insights from the psychedelic experience integration session: Verbatims differentiate 3-month abstinence in alcohol use disorder with depressive symptoms

items.title: The Ecstasy of Gold in Neurodiversity: Focus on the Use of Psychedelics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
items.summary_en: Review of psychedelics (serotonergic compounds including psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA) and their potential therapeutic applications in autism spectrum disorder. These substances may enhance cognitive function, brain connectivity, and neuroplasticity. While no authorized medications exist for core ASD symptoms, emerging studies suggest psychedelics could address specific aspects of autism-related difficulties, though further research is needed.

items.title: Acute dose-dependent effects of 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine (2C-B) compared with 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) and psilocybin in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study in healthy participants
items.summary_en: Acute dose-dependent effects of 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine (2C-B) compared with 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) and psilocybin in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study in healthy participants
items.notable_reason: First-in-human study for 2C-B with direct comparison to psilocybin and MDMA; double-blind RCT design with pharmacokinetic and neuroendocrine outcomes.

items.title: Rapid clinical improvement after intravenous ketamine in an adolescent with treatment-resistant depression, severe obesity, and pseudo-Cushing syndrome: A case report.
items.summary_en: Case report describing rapid clinical improvement in an adolescent with treatment-resistant depression following intravenous ketamine administration. The patient presented with comorbid severe obesity and pseudo-Cushing syndrome. This single case documents the therapeutic response but requires further investigation through controlled studies to establish efficacy and safety in this population.

items.title: Psilocybin as a Transdiagnostic Treatment for Eating Disorders and Comorbid Psychopathology: Implications for Clinical Nosology and Research Directions.
items.summary_en: A narrative review examines psilocybin as a transdiagnostic treatment for eating disorders and psychiatric comorbidities. Preliminary clinical evidence supports feasibility, safety, and therapeutic effects. Proposed mechanisms—serotonergic agonism, psychoplastogenic effects, neural desynchronization—target shared vulnerabilities across conditions, mapping onto HiTOP and RDoC dimensional frameworks. Future research should optimize trial design for this novel intervention approach.

items.title: Consensus by design: Conflict of interest and the intravenous ketamine Delphi guidelines.
items.summary_en: Critical analysis of the intravenous ketamine Delphi consensus guidelines, examining potential conflicts of interest in the expert panel and their influence on guideline development methodology.

items.title: Readability of informed consent forms from ClinicalTrials.gov in ketamine clinical trials for mental health conditions: a cross-sectional analysis.
items.summary_en: Cross-sectional analysis of 14 ketamine clinical trials examining readability of informed consent forms (ICFs) on ClinicalTrials.gov. ICFs averaged 5031 words requiring 21.4 minutes to read. Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level averaged 9.8 (13/14 documents above grade 8), indicating readability challenges for participants with cognitive or psychiatric symptoms.

items.title: Quarterly Psychedelics Briefing: Q2 2026
items.summary_en: Psychedelic Alpha's Q2 2026 quarterly briefing reviews major developments in hallucinogen research, drug development, policy, and regulation from the past three months. Editor Josh Hardman surveys progress across academia and industry, then forecasts upcoming trends for the next quarter.

items.title: Psychedelics and autism spectrum disorder: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence and ethical challenges.
items.summary_en: A narrative review examining psychedelics' potential in autism spectrum disorder treatment. While mechanistic evidence supports effects on serotonergic and glutamatergic signaling, neuroplasticity, and brain network reorganization, current clinical and preclinical data do not support direct treatment of core social communication deficits or repetitive behaviors. Psychedelics may benefit associated symptoms like anxiety and emotional dysregulation.

items.title: Patient-centred education for ketamine and esketamine therapies in mood disorders.
items.summary_en: Narrative review synthesizing evidence on patient education for ketamine and esketamine in treatment-resistant depression and bipolar depression. Identifies key information needs including indications, mechanisms, visit preparation, adverse effect management, and suicidality counselling. Proposes patient-centred psychoeducational framework addressing special populations.

items.title: Modeled Long-Term Effects of Psilocybin on Dynamic Activity and Effective Connectivity of Fronto-Striatal-Thalamic Circuits.
items.summary_en: Secondary fMRI analysis of psilocybin's long-term effects in healthy volunteers shows increased dynamic activity in fronto-striatal-thalamic circuits four weeks post-dose. Computational modeling suggests this involves reduced structure-function coupling and altered top-down/bottom-up modulation, linked to serotonergic and dopaminergic receptor availability. Findings support mechanistic understanding of psilocybin's sustained therapeutic effects.

items.title: Investigating the impact of serotonergic psychedelic drugs, MDMA and ketamine on social cognition in psychiatric disorders: A scoping review.
items.summary_en: Scoping review of 20 studies examining effects of ketamine, MDMA, psilocybin, LSD, and ayahuasca on social cognition in psychiatric disorders. Evidence suggests ketamine and psilocybin may modulate facial emotion processing in depression, while MDMA showed improvements in self-awareness and psychosocial functioning in PTSD. Direct evidence of clinical benefit remains limited.

items.title: Major depressive disorder-alcohol use disorder comorbidity: diagnosis, mechanisms and treatment.
items.summary_en: This review examines comorbid alcohol use disorder (AUD) and major depressive disorder (MDD), which occur together more frequently than other psychiatric-substance disorder combinations. Diagnostic criteria differ between DSM-5 and ICD-11. Underlying mechanisms include dysregulated reward processing, neuroinflammation, neurotransmitter imbalance, HPA axis dysfunction, and gut-brain axis disruption. Treatment approaches combine SSRIs with AUD-specific therapies, emerging agents like ketamine, and psychosocial interventions including CBT.

items.title: Study Protocol for "Exploring the safety and therapeutic potential of psilocybin in the treatment of anorexia nervosa in adolescents and young adults".
items.summary_en: Researchers are investigating psilocybin-assisted therapy for treatment-resistant anorexia nervosa in adolescents and young adults. This phase IIa randomized controlled trial will evaluate safety, tolerability, and feasibility of two psilocybin sessions combined with psychological support versus standard treatment alone in 16-35 year-olds with relapsing anorexia nervosa, examining clinical outcomes and neurobiological mechanisms.

items.title: Esketamine multi-omic biomarker evaluation in major depressive disorder (EMBER-MDD): concept, objectives and methodologies of a non-clinical investigator-initiated study.
items.summary_en: EMBER-MDD is a biomarker discovery study analyzing biological samples from patients with major depressive disorder to identify predictors of treatment resistance and molecular mechanisms underlying esketamine response. The research examines approximately 420 participants' blood samples using genomics, epigenomics, and transcriptomics to discover individual and integrated multi-omic signatures associated with treatment outcomes.

items.title: Excessive Switching in OCD and Paranoia Arises From Different Deficits in Belief-Updating.
items.summary_en: Obsessions and paranoia both involve cognitive inflexibility, but computational modeling of probabilistic reversal learning reveals distinct underlying mechanisms. While both conditions show excessive switching behavior, paranoia stems from deficits in updating reward beliefs, whereas obsessions involve different belief-updating impairments, enabling differential diagnosis beyond clinical interviews.

items.title: NMDA receptors are not necessary for burst firing of lateral habenula neurons in mice.
items.summary_en: Researchers found that NMDA receptors are not required for burst firing in lateral habenula neurons of mice. Since ketamine's antidepressant effects involve blocking this burst firing, alternative mechanisms beyond NMDA receptor inhibition may explain ketamine's rapid therapeutic action in depression treatment.

items.title: Optimized Oral Glutamatergic Augmentation in Refractory Home-Dominant Contamination Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder With Somatic, Affective, and Motivational Features: A Case Report of Incremental Functional Gains.
items.summary_en: A case report describes treatment of refractory contamination-focused obsessive-compulsive disorder using the Cheung glutamatergic regimen—an oral combination of dextromethorphan, CYP2D6 inhibition, piracetam, and L-glutamine designed to modulate glutamatergic signaling. A 26-year-old woman with persistent contamination fears, compulsive washing, and associated depression showed incremental functional improvements. The approach targets glutamatergic dysfunction as a potential mechanism in treatment-resistant OCD cases unresponsive to standard serotonergic and antipsychotic strategies.

items.title: Classical psychedelic microdosing, mood, and cognitive function: An umbrella review with narrative synthesis.
items.summary_en: Psychedelic microdosing (sub-perceptual LSD or psilocybin doses) has gained scientific interest for potential mood and cognitive benefits, but an umbrella review finds limited evidence. Current controlled studies do not support cognitive enhancement claims, though the review identifies methodological limitations and expectancy bias vulnerabilities in existing research.

items.title: The purpose of the psychosocial protocol in the psychedelic-assisted therapy: A scoping review.
items.summary_en: This scoping review categorizes psychosocial protocols in psychedelic-assisted psychiatric research by purpose, format, therapeutic orientation, formalization, and duration. The analysis examines studies involving ayahuasca, DMT, and other psychedelics, emphasizing the importance of structured psychological support alongside substance administration in treatment outcomes.

items.title: Psychological Adverse Effects of Psychedelic Use.
items.summary_en: This rounds report from Massachusetts General Hospital's Psychiatric Consultation Service examines adverse psychological effects associated with psychedelic use in hospitalized patients with comorbid psychiatric conditions, providing clinical guidance for practitioners managing complex cases at the medicine-psychiatry interface.

items.title: Medical Complications of Psychedelics.
items.summary_en: This rounds report from Massachusetts General Hospital's Psychiatric Consultation Service examines medical complications associated with psychedelics in hospitalized patients. The service addresses diagnostic and management challenges in cases where patients with complex medical or surgical conditions present concurrent psychiatric symptoms potentially related to psychedelic use.

items.title: An exploratory study of breathwork-induced altered states of consciousness in experienced practitioners: the airways to alteration (A2A) trial.
items.summary_en: A controlled study of 24 healthy adults compared high-ventilation breathwork to meditation for inducing altered states of consciousness. Breathwork produced significantly larger acute psychedelic-like effects, including greater oceanic boundlessness, emotional breakthrough, and insight than meditation. Results suggest breathwork may be a feasible non-pharmacological tool for ASC research, supporting future confirmatory trials.

items.title: Novel approaches in depression treatment: from rapid-acting antidepressants to personalized interventions.
items.summary_en: Research explores rapid-acting treatments for major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression, including psychedelics like psilocybin in late-stage trials, neuromodulation therapies such as FDA-cleared SAINT protocol, and biomarker-guided interventions like ALTO-300, representing progress toward personalized depression treatment options.

items.title: Increased morning cortisol after ketamine treatment for suicidal depression: Exploratory report from a randomized trial.
items.summary_en: Ketamine rapidly reduced suicidal ideation in depressed patients within 24 hours. Morning cortisol levels increased significantly after treatment, showing a small correlation with suicidal ideation reduction. These findings suggest moderate cortisol elevation may enhance stress resilience, though results require replication.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of orally administered S-ketamine in healthy participants.
items.summary_en: Oral S-ketamine shows poor bioavailability (9-12%) compared to intravenous administration due to first-pass metabolism, significantly reducing systemic exposure to S-ketamine and its active metabolites. A crossover study in healthy participants found that oral dosing alters pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles compared to IV administration, raising efficacy and safety concerns for treating depression.

items.title: The intersection between psychedelics and schizophrenia spectrum disorders: Reevaluating risk and therapeutic potential.
items.summary_en: This narrative review examines the relationship between psychedelics and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs), challenging the traditional "psychotomimetic" view that psychedelics simply mimic psychosis. While acknowledging overlapping phenomenological features and shared neural mechanisms involving serotonergic, dopaminergic, and glutamatergic systems, the authors identify important qualitative differences. Clinical evidence confirms psychedelics can exacerbate existing psychotic illness, yet the review suggests a more nuanced understanding is needed to properly assess therapeutic potential and risk in psychiatric populations.

items.title: Multi-metric evaluations of acute psychedelic effects on fMRI brain entropy.
items.summary_en: Study evaluating multiple brain entropy metrics in 28 participants receiving psilocybin found that five entropy measures consistently showed increased brain entropy, while eight showed no effect and one was inconsistent. Results support the theory that psychedelics increase brain entropy but suggest different metrics capture distinct neurobiological phenomena rather than a single construct.

items.title: Mechanistic insights toward dissociating therapeutic from psychedelic effects: bridging the gap between psychedelic research and mental health care.
items.summary_en: Psychedelics show promise for treating depression and anxiety, but their intense subjective effects—including ego dissolution and altered consciousness—require extensive support and limit accessibility. Researchers are exploring whether therapeutic benefits can be separated from consciousness-altering effects through pharmacological approaches targeting serotonin receptors, potentially improving scalability and clinical feasibility.

items.title: The Role of Monoacylglycerol Lipase (MAGL) in Substance Use: A Systematic Review of Preclinical Studies.
items.summary_en: MAGL, the primary enzyme regulating endocannabinoid system function, influences neurobiology relevant to substance use disorders. This systematic review of 42 preclinical studies examined whether substance exposure alters MAGL and whether manipulating MAGL affects addiction-related outcomes. Chronic exposure produced modest, region-specific changes: increased MAGL in hippocampus (alcohol), minimal striatal changes, and prefrontal cortex changes only after repeated stimulant exposure. Results suggest MAGL as a potential therapeutic target warrant further investigation.

items.title: Oral Prolonged-Release Ketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression: Two Randomized Clinical Trials.
items.summary_en: Researchers tested KET01, an oral prolonged-release ketamine formulation, for treating resistant depression. Two randomized trials compared it to esketamine and placebo across European sites. KET01 aims to provide ketamine's rapid antidepressant effects while reducing dissociative and cardiovascular side effects associated with existing ketamine treatments.

items.title: Sustained pharmacodynamic effects of S-ketamine on cortical excitability and resting-state brain activity: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
authors: de Cuba Catherine M K E
items.summary_en: S-ketamine demonstrates sustained effects on brain activity beyond acute administration. In a placebo-controlled crossover study, intravenous S-ketamine reduced motor responses and altered cortical inhibition patterns that persisted for up to seven days, measured via transcranial magnetic stimulation and electroencephalography. These biomarkers may help elucidate mechanisms underlying psychedelics' delayed antidepressant effects.

items.title: Evaluating the abuse liability of ketamine in the treatment of mood disorders: A systematic review.
items.summary_en: Systematic review of 30 studies examining ketamine's abuse potential in mood disorder treatment. Clinical evidence shows minimal craving, misuse, or dependence in supervised settings. Preclinical studies reveal differential abuse liability across ketamine forms: (S)-ketamine shows reward-related effects, racemic ketamine demonstrates reinforcement at higher doses, while (R)-ketamine shows minimal reinforcing properties. Overall findings suggest low abuse risk in controlled clinical contexts.

items.title: Intranasal esketamine in treatment-resistant depression with and without comorbid borderline personality disorder: A multicenter real-world longitudinal study.
items.summary_en: Intranasal esketamine effectively treats depression in both treatment-resistant depression (TRD) patients with and without comorbid borderline personality disorder. A real-world study of 90 TRD patients found both groups achieved similar remission rates (49-58%) at six months, though those with BPD showed faster early symptom improvement.

items.title: At-Home Telehealth-Supported Subcutaneous Ketamine Therapy in Adults With Moderate to Severe Depression, Anxiety, or PTSD: A Real-World Observational Study of Safety, Feasibility, and Clinical Outcomes in a Large, Heterogeneous Cohort in the United States.
items.summary_en: At-home telehealth-supported subcutaneous ketamine administration shows promise as an accessible treatment for depression, anxiety, and PTSD. This real-world study of 3,870 patients found subcutaneous delivery offers advantages over sublingual alternatives—superior bioavailability and precise dosing—while maintaining telehealth accessibility and reducing logistical barriers compared to in-clinic intravenous or intranasal approaches.

items.title: Psychedelic Use, Microdosing, Motives, and Information and Product Sources Among Young Adults in the United States.
items.summary_en: Survey of US young adults (18-34) examined correlates and motives for psychedelic use. Researchers analyzed patterns of psychedelic consumption, including microdosing practices, and identified various reasons driving use in this demographic. The study also investigated where users obtain information and products related to psychedelics, providing insights into sources and decision-making factors among young adult consumers.

items.title: Cannabis, Psychedelics, and Other Substance Use to Manage Premenstrual Symptoms: A Survey Study.
items.summary_en: A survey of 634 menstruating individuals examined substance use to manage premenstrual symptoms, including PMDD. Participants reported using cannabis, psychedelics, alcohol, and other substances across menstrual cycle phases. This represents the first assessment of psychedelic use patterns during the menstrual cycle, highlighting the need for rigorous clinical research on substance efficacy for premenstrual symptom management.

items.title: Clinical improvement following an integrative iboga microdosing protocol in post-concussive and hypoxic brain injury syndromes: a case series.
items.summary_en: A case series documents clinical improvements in three individuals with post-concussive or hypoxic-ischemic brain injury following a six-week iboga microdosing protocol (3.8-38.5 mg ibogaine-equivalent daily) combined with psychotherapy. This naturalistic study suggests psychedelics may offer therapeutic potential for persistent neurological symptoms resistant to conventional treatments.

items.title: Acute and post-acute neurobehavioral responses to lysergic acid diethylamide in healthy subjects: a randomized controlled study.
items.summary_en: This randomized controlled trial examined acute and post-acute effects of 100 µg LSD in 45 healthy subjects. Key findings include improved offline motor learning one day after dosing, reduced perceived stress and increased cognitive flexibility one week later. Neurophysiological assessments using EEG and TMS revealed acute changes in auditory processing. Results suggest psychedelics may produce lasting behavioral improvements in learning and cognitive function.

items.title: Meaning-Centered Psychotherapy for Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy Among Patients with Advanced Cancer and Depression: Rationale and Preliminary Evaluation of MCP-PSIL.
items.summary_en: Researchers developed Meaning-Centered Psychotherapy for Psilocybin (MCP-PSIL), a standardized five-session psychotherapeutic protocol combining psilocybin with meaning-centered psychotherapy for cancer patients with depression. Based on feedback from seven patients and six therapists who received psilocybin-assisted therapy followed by group meaning-centered psychotherapy, the study addresses gaps in evidence-based psychological preparation and integration protocols for psychedelic-assisted therapy.

items.title: Ketamine for the Treatment of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD): A Systematic Review on Efficacy and Tolerability.
items.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates ketamine's efficacy and safety for treating obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), a chronic condition causing intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors unresponsive to conventional treatments. Five studies using various administration routes and dosages demonstrated that ketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist, showed consistent and significant rapid-acting and enduring therapeutic effects for OCD patients.

items.title: Psychedelics, the media portrayal and large-language model evaluations.
items.summary_en: Research on psychedelics experienced decades of decline following 1960s backlash, but recently resurged alongside increased media coverage. Analysis of 25 years of media articles using large-language models revealed positive sentiment peaked in 2020, then declined sharply in 2024 after FDA rejected MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD—mirroring historical patterns. Sustained progress requires grounding therapeutic development in scientific evidence rather than media trends.

items.title: Psilocybin's kinematic effect on manual dexterity.
items.summary_en: Researchers assessed psilocybin's acute effects on manual dexterity using the Box and Block Test and kinematic analysis in healthy participants across multiple doses (5-20 mg). Results showed modest dose-dependent changes at higher doses, with slight impairment during peak effects and recovery by 4.5 hours, suggesting psilocybin's motor disruption is relatively mild and reversible.

items.title: Attitudes of Mental Healthcare Professionals Towards the Use of Psychedelics in the Treatment of Substance Use Disorders: A Systematic Review.
items.summary_en: A systematic review of six studies involving 966 mental healthcare professionals found that most hold cautiously optimistic views toward psychedelic-assisted therapy for treating substance use disorders. However, some expressed concerns about safety, efficacy, and clinical integration. Greater knowledge and familiarity with psychedelics predicted more positive attitudes among professionals.

items.title: Expectations and Motivations for Participation in Clinical Trials Utilizing Psychedelics for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Qualitative Study.
items.summary_en: Researchers interviewed 17 participants in psychedelic clinical trials for treatment-resistant depression to understand their motivations and expectations. Key motivations included hope, demoralization, prior experience, and social factors. Participants expected symptom reduction through mechanisms they perceived would occur during the psychedelic experience, emphasizing the importance of setting. Understanding these expectations is crucial, as they significantly shape trial outcomes and complicate interpretation of results through placebo effects.

items.title: Modulation of early non-rapid eye movement slow wave activity by ketamine in treatment-resistant depression.
items.summary_en: Ketamine increases slow-wave activity during early non-REM sleep in treatment-resistant depression patients, particularly those who respond to treatment. This study of 91 TRD patients and 42 healthy controls found baseline slow-wave deficits in depression, which ketamine but not placebo ameliorated, suggesting a mechanistic link between psychedelics' rapid antidepressant effects and sleep homeostasis restoration.

items.title: The claustrum as a central hub for reward and threat processing.
items.summary_en: The claustrum, a small conserved brain structure, emerges as a central hub integrating reward and threat processing. Recent research reveals its role in modulating both appetitive and aversive responses, with implications for understanding drug reward behaviors and defensive responses. This anatomical and functional review advances understanding of the claustrum's involvement in consciousness and psychedelic effects.

items.title: Increased brain VDAC1 protein levels correlate with behavioural performance in a ketamine murine model of schizophrenia and are attenuated by the mGluR2 modulator JNJ-46356479.
items.summary_en: Researchers found elevated VDAC1 protein levels in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of mice exposed to ketamine, a model of schizophrenia. These increases correlated with behavioral deficits. Treatment with JNJ-46356479, an mGluR2 modulator, reduced VDAC1 levels and improved behavioral outcomes, suggesting VDAC1 involvement in schizophrenia pathology via mitochondrial apoptosis dysregulation.

items.title: Predicting changes in depressive symptomatology following oral esketamine treatment in treatment-resistant depression: A machine-learning approach.
items.summary_en: Machine learning models were used to identify patient characteristics predicting antidepressant response to oral esketamine in treatment-resistant depression. Analysis of 131 patients receiving individualized doses twice weekly for six weeks found that early symptom improvement, alongside sociodemographic and clinical variables, could forecast outcomes in this population.

items.title: Hallucinogen-Assisted Psychotherapy for Trauma Disorders: A Bionian Lens.
items.summary_en: Researchers are investigating psychedelics like psilocybin and MDMA for treating trauma disorders. These substances produce profound experiences involving awe and connectedness. This article applies Bionian psychological concepts to neurobiological models, examining how trauma affects stress pathways and neural circuits, causing hyperarousal and rigid thinking, and how psychedelics may facilitate therapeutic change.

items.title: The Neurobiology of Trauma: Guest Editors' Introduction.
items.summary_en: This special issue explores the neurobiology of trauma, examining how traumatic experiences affect brain structure and function at the cellular and systems levels. The collection addresses mechanisms underlying trauma-related disorders and potential therapeutic interventions.

items.title: Psychodynamic Perspectives on Psychedelic States and Treatment Contexts: A Conceptual and Clinical Introduction.
items.summary_en: This article presents a psychodynamic framework for understanding psychedelic-assisted therapy, complementing existing neurobiological models. It examines how psychedelics facilitate access to unconscious material—preverbal, dissociated, and developmentally rooted content—expressed through somatic, symbolic, and affective experiences. The authors integrate psychoanalytic theory with clinical practice across screening, preparation, treatment, and integration phases, using illustrative case examples to demonstrate therapeutic applications for treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, addiction, and existential distress.

items.title: Ten practical suggestions for setting up a psychedelic study.
items.summary_en: Researchers face significant regulatory and logistical barriers when designing human psychedelic studies. This article offers practical guidance on study design, legal compliance, and drug procurement to help investigators establish rigorous mechanistic research needed to understand psychedelics' therapeutic potential across neuropsychiatric conditions, drawing on UK non-clinical study experience.

items.title: Psychedelic Therapy: A Primer for Primary Care Clinicians-Mescaline.
items.summary_en: Mescaline is a classic serotonergic psychedelic with indigenous ceremonial roots gaining renewed scientific interest for psychiatric applications. It acts primarily through 5-HT2A receptor agonism. While controlled studies in healthy volunteers show dose-dependent effects with transient autonomic stimulation and no serious complications, clinical trials in patient populations are lacking. Safety concerns remain regarding cardiovascular, metabolic, and psychiatric comorbidities, plus psychological risks and long-term therapeutic use.

items.title: Music Playlist Use in Clinical Trials of Psychedelic Assisted Psychotherapy: A Systematic Review.
items.summary_en: This systematic review examines how music is selected and used in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy across 36 clinical trials. Most studies combined music with psilocybin or MDMA to treat depression and PTSD, yet significant variation existed in music selection procedures. No standardized music protocol was identified, suggesting future research should establish guidelines for optimizing musical elements in psychedelic therapeutic settings.

items.title: Development and validation of a short-form (6-item) version of the clinician-administered dissociative states scale (CADSS-SF).
items.summary_en: Researchers developed and validated a 6-item short-form version of the Clinician Administered Dissociative States Scale (CADSS-SF) to assess transient dissociative states induced by psychedelics. Using nitrous oxide data from 229 healthy volunteers, they identified the most responsive items through factor analysis and validated the instrument with 80 additional participants. This briefer version reduces participant burden while enabling repeated assessments during psychedelic studies.

items.title: Treatment of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
items.summary_en: Expert consensus review of PTSD management identifies cognitive-behavioral therapy as most evidence-based psychotherapy, with virtual reality exposure emerging as promising. SSRIs and venlafaxine are first-line medications. Combined psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy generally outperform single treatments. Early prophylactic interventions lack evidence and may be harmful.

items.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder: pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, animal models, and potential therapeutic strategies.
items.summary_en: PTSD is a complex neurobehavioral disorder affecting 7% of U.S. adults and 12-30% of military personnel. Symptoms include memory loss, mood changes, anxiety, and depression. Pathophysiology involves HPA axis dysfunction, neural circuit abnormalities, neurochemical imbalances, neuroinflammation, and genetic factors. Current treatments combine pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy, though psychedelics show emerging therapeutic potential for treatment-resistant cases.

items.title: Pα+ Psychedelic Bulletin #226: The Ethics of Psilocybin for Advanced Alzheimer’s; Veterans’ Views on Psychedelics
items.summary_en: Recent case reports suggest psilocybin may benefit advanced Alzheimer's patients, generating significant media attention. However, researchers caution that single cases don't establish efficacy or safety in this vulnerable population. Ethical concerns include informed consent challenges and potential risks requiring careful clinical consideration before broader trials.

items.title: A Research Hypothesis, Not A Treatment Recommendation: Marcos Lago on the Viral Psilocybin for Alzheimer’s Case Report
items.summary_en: Marcos Lago discusses a viral case report suggesting psilocybin's potential for Alzheimer's disease. He emphasizes this represents preliminary research observations rather than established treatment evidence, cautioning against premature clinical applications while supporting continued scientific investigation into psychedelics' neurobiological effects.

items.title: ‘A Sea Change’, With Caveats: A Closer Look at Definium’s Phase 3 LSD for MDD Readout
items.summary_en: Definium Therapeutics reported positive Phase 3 trial results for DT120, an LSD-based treatment for major depressive disorder. The announcement drove significant stock appreciation and $700M funding plans, though detailed data analysis reveals important caveats to the seemingly optimistic topline results.

items.title: Breaking: Definium Lands Positive Phase 3, LSD Candidate Shows Strong Antidepressant Effect
items.summary_en: Definium Therapeutics announced positive Phase 3 results for DT120, an LSD-based treatment for major depressive disorder, marking the first Phase 3 data for LSD in clinical development and demonstrating strong antidepressant efficacy.

items.title: Psilocybin Compassionate Use in Germany: Lea Mertens and Andrea Jungaberle on the First Patients, Payers and Practicalities
items.summary_en: Germany approved the EU's first psilocybin compassionate use program, allowing two centers to administer psilocybin to patients. The initiative, overseen by OVID Clinic Berlin and another institution, represents a regulatory milestone enabling access to psychedelics for eligible patients outside standard clinical trials.

items.title: May 2026 Psychedelic Bill Roundup
items.summary_en: In 2026, legislators tracked 115 psychedelics-related bills, with 17 signed into law. May saw over a quarter of signings as legislative sessions concluded, marking peak policy reform activity for the year across state and federal levels.

items.title: Pα+ Psychedelic Bulletin #225: Q1 Lobbying Update; Individual vs. Group MDMA Therapy Study Launches; Australia Loosens Psychedelics Access Regulations; VA Launches “New” MDMA Trial
items.summary_en: Recent psychedelic developments include increased Q1 lobbying efforts, launch of studies comparing individual versus group MDMA therapy, Australia's relaxed psychedelics access regulations, and a new VA MDMA trial. The field shows expanding research activity and regulatory momentum across multiple jurisdictions.

items.title: A Dispatch from APA’s Annual Meeting: Psychedelics Return at an Awkward Moment for American Psychiatry
items.summary_en: Psychedelics gained prominent visibility at the American Psychiatric Association's annual meeting, reflecting the field's struggle to integrate these emerging therapeutics into mainstream psychiatry amid broader questions about psychiatry's role in American society.
